title: 01. Foundations: Transformer Architecture
summary: Transformer is the neural network architecture that powers ALL modern LLMs.

sections.title: 4.1 What is a Transformer?
sections.body:
### The Big Picture First
> **Transformer is the neural network architecture that powers ALL modern LLMs.**

Before Transformers (pre-2017), AI used older architectures (RNNs, LSTMs) that were slow and couldn't handle long texts well.

In **2017**, Google published a paper called **"Attention is All You Need"** → This introduced the Transformer → It changed everything.

### Simple Analogy: The Reading Comprehension Expert

Imagine reading this sentence:
> *"The animal didn't cross the street because **it** was too tired."*

What does "**it**" refer to? → The **animal**!

Now try:
> *"The animal didn't cross the street because **it** was too wide."*

What does "**it**" refer to now? → The **street**!

A Transformer can figure this out because it uses **ATTENTION** — it looks at ALL words in a sentence simultaneously and figures out which words are related to each other.

```
│                                                  │

│  └─────────────┘                                 │
│       ↓                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐             │
│  │    ATTENTION LAYERS (x N)       │             │
│  │                                 │             │
│  │  • Self-Attention               │             │
│  │  • Multi-Head Attention         │             │
│  │  • Feed-Forward Network         │             │
```

sections.title: 4.3 The ATTENTION Mechanism (The Magic Ingredient)
sections.body:
### What Problem Does Attention Solve?

Old systems read text like a conveyor belt — left to right, one word at a time, often forgetting earlier words.

Attention says: **"When processing word X, which OTHER words in the sentence should I pay attention to?"**

### Visual Example

Sentence: **"The cat sat on the mat because it was comfortable"**

When processing the word **"it"**:
```
The   cat   sat   on   the   mat   because   it   was   comfortable
 5%   85%   2%   1%    2%    5%      0%      -    0%       0%
```
The model pays **85% attention** to "cat" → it knows "it" = "cat" ✅

### Types of Attention
| Type | What It Does |
|------|-------------|
| **Self-Attention** | Words attend to other words in the SAME sentence |
| **Cross-Attention** | Words in output attend to words in input (translation) |
| **Multi-Head Attention** | Multiple attention operations in parallel (catches different relationships) |

sections.title: 4.4 Encoder vs Decoder vs Encoder-Decoder
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   3 TYPES OF TRANSFORMERS                │
├────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────────────┤
│   ENCODER      │    DECODER     │  ENCODER-DECODER       │
│   ONLY         │    ONLY        │  (Seq2Seq)             │
├────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
│ Reads &        │ Generates      │ Reads input &          │
│ understands    │ text token     │ generates output       │
│ text           │ by token       │                        │
├────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
│ Good for:      │ Good for:      │ Good for:              │
│ Classification │ Text           │ Translation            │
│ Embeddings     │ Generation     │ Summarization          │
│ Search         │ Chatbots       │ Q&A                    │
├────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
│ Examples:      │ Examples:      │ Examples:              │
```
